description: Reliability PR 5's second English set, made after the first set's held-out half was revealed and the host-model fallback was added: the 72 calibration intents of `eval/jev/reliability/intents.json` verbatim (review r1), and 72 held-out intents written fresh (review r2), six per family in the first set's held-out strata, over the same Kestrel corpus plus pages only they name. No first-set page is edited, so every calibration intent's source hashes still hold. Fields mean what they mean in the first set.

r1.note: A model review, not a human one, at the repository owner's direction: five rounds before any held-out run (round 1 by luna 6.0, rounds 2-5 by gpt-6-sol, whose round 3 read every intent); every finding was fixed before the re-freeze.

r2.note: The fresh held-out half and the pages only it names, a model review at the repository owner's direction: three rounds by gpt-6-sol before any v2 run (round 1: three references trimmed to what their questions ask, five bridge targets reworded to remove lexical shortcuts; round 2: bridge-15 reworded; round 3: nothing found). Approved inputs: intents 0321f73a, actions c0b0f55d.

files.repo/docs/overview.md:
# Kestrel overview

Kestrel archives signed event batches from product services and replays them on request.

files.hub/craft/short-branches.md:
# Short-lived branches

Rule. A feature branch is merged or closed within five working days of its first commit.
files.hub/operator/deploy-announcements.md:
# Deploy announcements

Rule. Every production deploy is announced in #deploys before it starts.
files.hub/craft/config-from-env.md:
# Configuration

Rule. Configuration is read from environment variables at start-up; no service reads config files at runtime.
files.hub/craft/api-deprecation.md:
# API deprecation

Rule. A public API field is deprecated for at least 90 days before it is removed.
files.hub/craft/metric-names.md:
# Metric names

Rule. Metric names are snake_case, prefixed with kestrel_, with the unit as a suffix.
files.hub/craft/no-bare-except.md:
# No bare except

Rule. Never catch every exception; catch the specific ones the code can handle.
files.hub/craft/test-names.md:
# Test names

Rule. A test's name states the behaviour it checks, not the function it calls.
files.hub/craft/named-constants.md:
# Named constants

Rule. A number with a meaning gets a named constant; only 0, 1 and -1 may appear bare.
files.hub/operator/commit-messages.md:
# Commit messages

Rule. A commit subject is in the imperative mood and at most 72 characters.
files.hub/craft/todo-issues.md:
# TODO comments

Rule. A TODO comment names an issue number; a TODO without one is refused in review.
files.hub/craft/input-validation.md:
# Input validation

Rule. Request input is validated at the API boundary; a rejected request gets a 400 naming the failing field.

papers.dpr.md:
# Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

Karpukhin et al. (2020) train two BERT encoders, one for questions and one for passages, and score a pair by the dot product of their vectors. Training uses in-batch negatives plus one hard negative per question retrieved by BM25. On Natural Questions, top-20 retrieval accuracy rose from 59.1% with BM25 to 78.4%.
papers.rag.md:
# Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

Lewis et al. (2020) combine a pre-trained retriever (DPR) with a BART generator. RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved passage for the whole output sequence; RAG-Token may draw on a different passage for each generated token.
papers.fid.md:
# Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering

Izacard and Grave (2021) propose Fusion-in-Decoder: each retrieved passage is encoded independently together with the question, and the decoder attends over the concatenation of all encoded passages. Accuracy kept rising as the number of passages grew to 100.
papers.react.md:
# ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

Yao et al. (2023) prompt a language model to interleave reasoning traces with task-specific actions, such as queries to a Wikipedia API, so that reasoning steers the actions and the observations inform the reasoning.
papers.colbert.md:
# ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT

Khattab and Zaharia (2020) encode the query and the passage separately into one embedding per token, and score a pair by summing, over the query tokens, each token's maximum similarity to any passage token (late interaction).
